$comment: Native components that are compiled into the shipped application and therefore appear in NOTICE.
They are not in package-lock.json because they are not npm packages: MuPDF is downloaded as source,
hash-verified, and statically linked into native/mupdf-shim by scripts/provision/mupdf.mjs.
MuPDF's own version is NOT restated here. generateNotice.mjs imports MUPDF_VERSION from the
provisioning script, so the pin has one home and the NOTICE cannot claim a version nobody built.
The bundled list below is what the PROJECT REFERENCE GRAPH from libmupdf.vcxproj compiles,
taken from source-file paths only. Three earlier readings were each wrong, in both directions:
1. thirdparty/'s directory listing — over-declares. It ships sources for targets we do not
build (curl, freeglut, zint, zxing-cpp).
2. A list written by hand from the spike's prose — under-declares.
3. Any `thirdparty\X` mention in libmupdf.vcxproj — over-declares AND under-declares at once.
It matched AdditionalIncludeDirectories, which names thirdparty\openssl\include and
thirdparty\libarchive\include — directories the 1.28.0 tarball does not even contain — so
OpenSSL entered a licence notice for a library the build has never seen. And libmupdf.vcxproj
compiles only MuPDF's own source/**, so every bundled library arriving through a referenced
project was invisible: tesseract and leptonica are statically linked and were both missed.
Confirmed against the shipped 42 MB DLL: `?AVTessErrStream@tesseract@@` is present as a mangled
C++ type, and no OpenSSL banner, SSLeay string or EVP_ symbol appears anywhere in it.
It is a declaration rather than a scan because the source is only present on a machine that has
provisioned it, and a NOTICE generable only there would be generated rarely.
checkNativeComponents() in generateNotice.mjs parses the vcxproj whenever the source IS present,
so the declaration cannot drift from the build in silence — the native CI job is where that runs.

components.name: MuPDF
components.role: PDF parsing, rendering and writing engine. Statically linked into the shim.
$licences: Read from each library's own licence file in the provisioned source tree, not from a
package index. Every one is permissive or AGPL, so all are compatible with this project's
AGPL-3.0-or-later. No component forces a stricter term than MuPDF already does.
The zint entry is the one that needed checking rather than assuming, because zint is two
things under one name: its LICENSE records that in 2013 the BACKEND was relicensed to BSD
expressly so it could be linked into other products, while the frontends and the Qt4
backend stayed GPL. libzxing.vcxproj compiles 101 files and every one is under
thirdparty/zint/backend — no frontend, no backend_qt, no backend_tcl. A GPL-2-only
component would have been a genuine conflict in an AGPL-3 project; this is not one.
FreeType is the one genuinely DUAL-licensed component, and a notice records the option
TAKEN rather than the options available — a downstream redistributor needs to know which
terms bind them, and for a dual licence that follows from our choice, not from the menu.
We take the FreeType License. FreeType's own text is explicit that the two are 'mutually
exclusive' and that 'you must choose one', and that the FTL is compatible with GPL-3 but
NOT GPL-2 — so the alternative, GPL-2-or-later, is the branch that could conflict with
AGPL-3 depending on how a redistributor versions it. FTL cannot.
The FTL carries an advertising clause requiring the FreeType project to be cited
explicitly in the product's documentation. This file and the generated NOTICE are that
citation, which is why FreeType appears by name rather than folded into a count.
Checked for the same shape across all sixteen, by scanning each licence file for
choice-of-licence wording rather than by recalling which projects are dual-licensed.
FreeType is the only one. The hits on extract and jbig2dec are AGPL's ordinary '(at your
option) any later version' clause, which is a version range and not a choice of terms;
the hits on harfbuzz and zint were build instructions in READMEs.
harfbuzz is a composite rather than a dual: its COPYING states the whole is 'Old MIT' and
that individual subdirectories may carry their own COPYING. That needs no choice from us —
every part binds at once — and it is recorded with that caveat named.

licences.freetype: FreeType License (FTL) — the option taken; see the note above
licences.harfbuzz: MIT ("Old MIT"); some subdirectories carry their own COPYING
licences.zint: BSD-3-Clause — backend only, which is all that is compiled
